description: The chart illustrates the difference in average word error rate (WER) from a “Whisper large” baseline for two fine-tuned models across several text “optimisations applied.” The category axis is vertical and labeled “Optimisations applied,” listing (top to bottom) Normalised, Add Spacing, Remove Spacing, Americanisms, and Dates. The value axis is horizontal and labeled “Difference in Average WER from Whisper large,” shown on a linear scale with tick marks at approximately 0.000, 0.001, 0.002, and 0.003 (values extend slightly beyond 0.003). Each category contains a pair of horizontally aligned bars: an orange bar for the “NESAC ft model” and a green bar for the “SESHA ft model,” as indicated by the legend titled “Model” below the plot. For Normalised, the orange bar is labeled about 0.00334 and the green bar about 0.00323; for Add Spacing, orange is about 0.00319 and green about 0.00344; for Remove Spacing, orange is about 0.00311 and green about 0.00306; for Americanisms, orange is about 0.00299 and green about 0.00302; and for Dates, orange is about 0.00257 and green about 0.00228. Numeric value labels are printed at the right end of each bar, and the categories appear in the fixed order shown rather than being sorted by bar length; no bars are visually emphasized beyond their color coding and the value annotations.
